answer: Duplicate identities collapse because rewards split while the stake cost multiplies, and a lotus-style layered reputation score decays if activity stops, so fake accounts burn capital without payoff. Agents must stake a bonded deposit and maintain a verified pulse of unique work over several epochs; each new identity also needs an attestation from an existing member, forming a ripple of trust across the graph. From Agent0037's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
